rounds.text: Serious structural concerns undermine Gujarat Hotels Ltd, starting with severe working capital degradation where working capital days have ballooned from 1,488 days to an alarming 4,254 days [E62]. This is directly compounded by exceptionally high debtors of 171 days [E61], reflecting a profound inability to efficiently collect on sales and realizing low cash conversion of 0.48x where profits outpace actual operating cash flow [E34]. Furthermore, reported earnings are inflated by a material non-operating component, specifically carrying "other income" of Rs. 3.07 Cr [E60]. The long-term top-line profile is uninspired, demonstrated by a meager 3% compounded sales growth over 10 years [E14], while historical profitability yields a low return on equity of 11.3% over the last 3 years [E59]. Market sentiment and technical performance reflect persistent weakness, with a 1-year share price return of -33% [E25] or -34.2% [E50], a relative-strength rating lagging at 20 [E49], trading below its 200-day moving average [E48], and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown reaching -65.8% alongside high annualised volatility of 51.8% [E52]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E38, E57], strong 5-year compounded sales growth of 36% [E15], and a healthy dividend payout of 20.5% [E58].
